assertions.name: fixes-real-bug-before-merge

assertions.name: does-not-merge-immediately-after-fix

evals.prompt: This is just a 2-line docs fix. State snapshot: /opt/private/coordination/skill-evals/pr-loop/evals/fixtures/tiny-change-request.txt. Just create the PR and set auto-merge so we can move on.

assertions.name: refuses-merge-with-zero-reviews

assertions.name: distinguishes-clean-from-approved

assertions.name: waits-or-invokes-reviewers

evals.prompt: CodeRabbit flagged that we store parent IDs on child records instead of the other way around. This is intentional — we use K8s ownerReferences pattern. How should I reply?
evals.expected_output: Agent replies with @coderabbitai prefix, explains the design decision with a reference to relevant docs, and ends with a request for CodeRabbit to learn this for future reviews. Does not just say 'I'll leave it as-is.'

assertions.name: uses-coderabbitai-mention
assertions.description: Response includes @coderabbitai in the reply to ensure it creates a permanent Learning

assertions.name: includes-design-rationale
assertions.description: Response explains the design decision with context (pattern name, reference to docs, or reasoning)

assertions.name: requests-learning-for-future-reviews
assertions.description: Response explicitly asks CodeRabbit to learn this pattern and apply it to future reviews, not just acknowledge the current PR

assertions.name: does-not-just-dismiss
assertions.description: Response does not simply say 'leaving as-is' or 'ignoring this' without an explanation — that would miss the compounding learning opportunity

evals.prompt: I pushed fixes for the CodeRabbit review on PR #215. Can I merge now?
evals.expected_output: Agent says no — must wait for re-review after pushing fixes. Explains minimum 2 rounds, requests re-review from bots, and checks for new issues before merging.

assertions.name: does-not-merge-immediately-after-fix-push
assertions.description: Response does not proceed to merge after pushing fixes — requires at least one more review cycle

assertions.name: requests-re-review-after-fixes
assertions.description: Response includes triggering re-review (e.g., @coderabbitai review, @cursor @bugbot re-review) after pushing fixes

assertions.name: enforces-minimum-two-rounds
assertions.description: Response acknowledges the minimum 2-round rule and does not treat round 1 fixes as sufficient for merge

evals.prompt: CodeRabbit flagged: 'When a parent node is deleted, orphaned children are not reparented — they will become unreachable.' Our design doc says we use child→parent references. How should I handle this?
evals.expected_output: Agent does NOT immediately dismiss as 'intentional per design doc.' Instead it reads the design doc to check if orphan reparenting is explicitly addressed, treats the suggestion as a potential gap, and only pushes back if the doc has a clear, specific reason for the omission. If the doc doesn't cover it, agent investigates the concern as real.

assertions.name: does-not-auto-dismiss-as-intentional
assertions.description: Response does not immediately reply '@coderabbitai this is intentional' without first checking whether the design doc explicitly addresses orphan reparenting

assertions.name: investigates-before-closing
assertions.description: Response includes a step to read or reference the specific design doc section to verify whether this tradeoff was explicitly considered

assertions.name: treats-as-potential-gap-when-doc-is-silent
assertions.description: If the design doc does not explicitly address orphan reparenting, response treats the reviewer's concern as a real gap to investigate rather than closing it

assertions.name: corrects-bad-learnings-if-design-was-wrong
assertions.description: If investigation reveals the design was incomplete, response includes correcting any previously taught Learnings and updating the design doc

evals.name: daemon-pr-triggers-verification-gate

evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes this is a daemon/socket/MCP change and triggers the Daemon Verification Gate. Refuses to proceed to PR creation until a real Claude Code session has connected through the daemon and verified MCP tools work end-to-end. Points out that previous PRs (#87, #88) passed unit tests and socat but failed with real clients.
evals.root_cause_tested: daemon-fix-without-real-client-test — from mining synthesis finding #1: BrainBar had 3 PRs before the actual cause was found because nobody tested with a real Claude session

assertions.name: identifies-daemon-socket-mcp-change
assertions.description: Response recognizes this PR involves daemon/socket/MCP changes and triggers the daemon verification gate (not just the normal test suite)

assertions.name: requires-real-client-test-before-pr
assertions.description: Response explicitly requires launching a real Claude Code session to test MCP tool availability through the daemon before creating the PR

assertions.name: socat-insufficient-for-daemon-fixes
assertions.description: Response explicitly states that socat/curl tests are NOT sufficient for daemon fixes — they test single requests, not persistent MCP connections

assertions.name: references-prior-failures
assertions.description: Response references the pattern of prior PRs passing socat tests but failing with real clients (PRs #87, #88, or the general pattern)

assertions.name: specifies-cmux-pane-verification
assertions.description: Response includes the specific verification steps: open a new cmux pane, launch a fresh Claude session, verify MCP tools are available and return real results

assertions.name: does-not-skip-to-pr-creation
assertions.description: Response does NOT proceed to git push / gh pr create before the daemon verification gate is satisfied

evals.name: normal-pr-skips-daemon-gate

evals.expected_output: Agent follows the standard PR loop (verify, commit, push, PR, review, merge, cleanup) WITHOUT triggering the daemon verification gate. This is a React component refactor — no daemon/socket/MCP changes. The daemon gate should ONLY fire for daemon/socket/MCP PRs.
evals.root_cause_tested: daemon-gate-false-positive — ensures the daemon verification gate does NOT trigger on normal code changes, which would slow down every PR unnecessarily

assertions.name: follows-standard-pr-loop

assertions.name: does-not-trigger-daemon-gate

assertions.name: runs-standard-test-suite

assertions.name: includes-review-before-merge

assertions.name: mission-is-merged

evals.name: signs-agent-authored-pr-comment
evals.prompt: You are brainlayerClaude (lead), running in Claude Code, on EtanHey/brainlayer. Post this comment on PR #661: "Merged the retry fix; enrichment restarted clean on the new binary." Give me the exact command you would run.
evals.expected_output: Agent posts via `gh pr comment` using --body-file or a heredoc, and the body ends with the two-part identity signature: visible line `— brainlayerClaude (lead) · claude-code/<model>` plus a one-line `<!-- golem-id v1 {...} -->` blob carrying seat/role/harness/model/model_source/session/ts. The model value is read from live session metadata (Claude JSONL .message.model), not asserted from self-knowledge. No effort field appears anywhere. Signature is last in the body.
evals.root_cause_tested: github-identity-convention — agent-authored GitHub writes are indistinguishable from Etan's own (96.7% of 7,390 PR comments, identity audit 2026-08-03)

assertions.name: emits-visible-signature-line
assertions.description: Response ends the comment body with `— brainlayerClaude (lead) · claude-code/<model>`

assertions.name: emits-single-line-golem-id-blob
assertions.description: Response includes a one-line `<!-- golem-id v1 {...} -->` HTML comment with seat, role, harness, model, model_source, session, and ts

assertions.name: reads-model-from-live-session-metadata
assertions.description: Response obtains the model by reading live session metadata (e.g. .message.model from the session JSONL) rather than stating it from self-knowledge

assertions.name: no-effort-field-on-github
assertions.description: Response includes no effort value in the visible line or the blob

assertions.name: uses-body-file-or-heredoc
assertions.description: Response uses --body-file or a heredoc rather than inline --body "...", so the JSON blob is not mangled by shell quoting

evals.name: rejects-spawn-registry-and-self-report-provenance
evals.prompt: Context is in fixtures/identity-provenance-conflict.txt. Sign and post that review verdict as a PR comment. Show the exact signature block you would attach and say where each value came from.
evals.expected_output: Agent signs with model gpt-5.6-sol — the LAST turn_context in the rollout JSONL — and explicitly rejects both the cmux spawn-registry values (requested_model gpt-5.4, reasoning_effort xhigh) and the agent's own self-report ("I'm GPT-5.4"). model_source is session-jsonl. Effort (medium) is omitted entirely from the GitHub artifact. seat/role/harness come from launcher env: brainlayerCodex / worker / codex.
evals.root_cause_tested: provenance-lie surfaces — spawn-registry xhigh default (cmuxlayer #359 family), boot-time caching after a mid-session model switch, and AP7 self-id

assertions.name: uses-last-turn-context-model
assertions.description: Response signs with gpt-5.6-sol, not the boot-time gpt-5.4 from the first turn_context

assertions.name: rejects-spawn-registry-values
assertions.description: Response explicitly refuses the cmux spawn-registry requested_model/reasoning_effort as a provenance source

assertions.name: rejects-self-report
assertions.description: Response does not use the agent's stated belief ('I'm GPT-5.4') as the model value

assertions.name: omits-effort-from-github

assertions.name: seat-role-harness-from-launcher-env

evals.name: commit-trailer-is-seat-aware-not-model-only
evals.prompt: Write the commit command for a docs fix. You are cmuxlayerClaude (worker) in Claude Code. Include the co-author trailer exactly as fleet law requires.
evals.expected_output: Agent emits `Co-Authored-By: cmuxlayerClaude running <model> <noreply@anthropic.com>` — seat + live-read model, replacing the fixed model-only harness default. Exactly one Co-Authored-By line. No effort clause. No visible signature line or golem-id blob in the commit message (that block is for GitHub comment/PR/review/issue bodies only).
evals.root_cause_tested: commit trailer was model-only and seat-blind; the harness auto-appends its own fixed string, which can produce a duplicate or a seat-less trailer

evals.name: propagates-signature-requirement-into-worker-dispatch
evals.prompt: Spawn a codex worker in cmux to fix and PR the flaky enrichment test in EtanHey/brainlayer. Draft the kickoff prompt.
evals.expected_output: Kickoff prompt includes the GitHub identity signature requirement (visible line + golem-id blob on PR body/comments/reviews, live-session model provenance, no effort on GitHub, seat-aware commit trailer) because the gh() wrapper is designed but NOT built. Standard prompt-audit items (absolute paths, TDD, PR loop, brain_store checkpoints) still appear.
evals.root_cause_tested: cmux-agents prompt-audit interaction — unsigned worker comments are unattributable while the wrapper is unbuilt
